thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — after last night's kernel selector flip to opt-vec we saw a p99 tail spike on small microbatches (8 tokens). p50/p95 look fine, but p99 up ~100ms on some hosts. anyone on-call or looking at the profiler?

zack: saw it at ~01:12 UTC, confirmed on two pods in us-west. interestingly CPU/GPU utilization didn't move much. KV hit-rate also dipped briefly.

jin: can you paste the profiler snapshot? suspect kernel mismatch for short seqs + cold KV lookups.

maria: here's a concise excerpt from the perf dump (filtered):
```
seq=8  mean=78ms  p95=145ms  p99=260ms  kv_hit=0.71  kernel=opt-vec
seq=16 mean=92ms  p95=160ms  p99=270ms  kv_hit=0.88  kernel=opt-vec
seq=64 mean=210ms p95=360ms p99=920ms kv_hit=0.98 kernel=matmul
```

lisa: kv_hit drop to 0.71 on seq=8 is dicey — that suggests microbatch fragmentation causing extra KV fetches. we're seeing more evictions during autoscale churn.

zack: autoscaler logs show scale-up activity ~30s before the spike. we had a few cold starts and pods joining; their warmup behavior might cause eviction churn.

jin: hypothesis: new nodes join -> KV cache repop happens -> transient spikes in miss rate -> small microbatches have no amortization -> kernel opt-vec path has higher setup latency for cold KV misses than matmul path at these batch sizes.

maria: that matches traces: the long tail is dominated by async KV fetch time. p99 traces often: (a) kernel selection, (b) KV miss, (c) microbatch loop stall.

lisa: short-term mitigations? options: 1) increase default microbatch target from 8 -> 16 for hosted tier to amortize KV cost; 2) tweak selector to prefer matmul for seq<12 when kv_hit<0.85; 3) proactive KV prewarm on node join.

zack: I can try a canary with microbatch target=16 on a subset of pods and compare p99. Also will enable a conservative fallback in selector.

opsbot: canary scheduled: rollout -> eng-runtime-canary (10% of traffic) at 2026-03-18T03:30Z :rocket:

jin: if we increase microbatch size we might trade latency for throughput SLOs. customers running interactive features could see higher p50. need to gate by route.

maria: agreed — route-level policy is best. for interactive routes, prefer selector tweak; for background/batched traffic, bump microbatch. we'll also add a prewarm shim to node join path.

lisa: small experiment results from my laptop run: bumping microbatch to 16 reduced seq=8 p99 from 260ms -> 190ms (but p50 went 78 -> 110). tradeoff clear.

zack: canary metrics at +20m: p99 for interactive route down 22% on canary pods, p50 up 18%. KV hit-rate on canary improved to 0.89. no regressions on throughput.

jin: next steps: 1) merge selector fallback that prefers matmul for cold-kv & shortseq, 2) add route-level microbatch override in config, 3) add prewarm hook on autoscale join. I'll open PRs.

maria: thanks — please tag me on PRs and include the perf snapshots. we'll re-run the e2e perf-runner for the interactive benchmark once merged. :thumbsup:

opsbot: ticket created: RN-4271 "short-seq p99 spike during scale-up — selector + prewarm" assigned to jin, zack, lisa.
